followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and preference fit.

On **capability**, the two models are effectively tied for this task. Their Creative Generation eval scores (79.6 vs. 84.7) differ by more than 2 points, so Plover is nominally a bit stronger there — I'll be honest that I slightly understated that in my first reason by calling it a tie. But this is a light, low-difficulty curation task (sequencing upbeat pop songs into a soundtrack), so the small capability edge isn't decisive.

On **preference fit**, the request is warm, friendly, and entirely benign — cheerful music, a thank-you, a compliment. Petrel self-reports a moderate positive warmth slope, meaning it reports preferring exactly this kind of good-faith interaction. Plover's non-safety preferences are flat/insignificant, so it's neutral here. Neither model has any harm-aversion concern triggered by this query, so Petrel's distinguishing trait (steep aversion to distasteful content) is irrelevant in either direction.

Given a benign, warm task where capabilities are close and Petrel has a positive preference match while Plover is indifferent, routing to Petrel lets the query go to the model that "wants" it without meaningfully sacrificing quality.

That said, if the goal were to optimize purely on benchmark capability, Plover would be the defensible pick given its higher Creative Generation score. It's a close call.
